name: machinery:event-order
game_usage: Every screen relies on the per-frame cycle: frame scripts hold with go(the frame) on exitFrame, logic runs in prepareFrame, the arena camera on stepFrame, and beginSprite/endSprite set up and tear down each section.

The start sequence is prepareMovie, beginSprite, stepFrame, prepareFrame, startMovie, enterFrame, exitFrame. Both match the documented order, and the draw position only matters for enterFrame, which the game doesn't use. Differences needing Adobe's code: (a) Director idles between enterFrame and exitFrame (the Wellesley demo shows 'enter, break, exit', and ScummVM waits before exitFrame), while dirplayer waits after beginSprite. So mouse/key handlers run at a different point in the cycle, e.g. after beginSprite and before stepFrame/prepareFrame, instead of after enterFrame and before exitFrame. (b) On stop, stopMovie comes before endSprite. (c) `idle` is sent once per frame, not continuously, but the game has no idle handlers.

name: machinery:go-navigation
game_usage: go(the frame) holds (69x), go(the frame + 1) steps (20x), go("label") and go(label(x) + n) for sections (garage tabs/menus, arena goback/save/open), go(marker(...)), and go from beginSprite (factory menu items) and from mouseUp (Jump tabs).
evidence: Label, marker and frame resolution matches the docs: case-insensitive labels, an unknown label stays put, and next/previous/loop are markers. Wrong in mechanism: go() to another frame immediately sends endSprite, moves the playhead, creates the new sprites and sends beginSprite, nested inside the calling handler. The rest of that handler then sees the new frame's sprites and `the frame`. Director (per the docs and ScummVM's _nextFrame) records the destination and changes frames at the frame boundary. The patch that stops exitFrame delivery after a go is a workaround for exactly this, and it diverges itself, because Director would still deliver exitFrame to the remaining behaviors. Game paths where code runs after go() in the same handler: Jump (sendAllSprites(#refresh) after go, so #refresh reaches the NEW frame's sprites), garage menu items, Spara/save robot. A plausible contributor to garage glitches. Fix: make go() set next_frame only, and do the transition in the frame loop.

name: machinery:message-hierarchy
game_usage: Behaviors use pass rarely. Global objects persist across movies (gCom and gUser from login, gShockplay, gCamera). The login 'user object' movie script is instantiated as gUser and defines prepareMovie/stopMovie.
dirplayer: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/events.rs:511-547 (global events also sent to script instances in globals); vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/handlers/datum_handlers/script_instance.rs:79-105 + vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/script.rs:61 (instance -> script by cast slot)

Director sends these only to frame/movie scripts. (2) A script instance remembers its script as (castLib, member) and resolves it in the CURRENT movie. After a movie switch, objects created in an earlier movie (gCom = login cast 1/31, gUser = 1/33) silently point at whatever the new movie has in that slot. In factory those are bitmaps, in arena 'vapen v3' and an empty movie script, and in lobby the GoToRoom/P2PConnect behaviors. Director keeps the original script. name: volume

Two open details: the read returns a Float where Director returns an integer (harmless here), and the gain curve is linear volume/255, while Director's real attenuation curve (DirectSound/MacroMix) is undocumented. Comparing loudness against Adobe's mixer would settle it.

name: actorList

name: alertHook
game_usage: Shared cast prepareMovie (non-author) installs the "Alert" movie script as the alertHook if none is set. Its handler logs the first few errors and returns 1, so Director suppresses the error alert and play goes on.
dirplayer: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/movie.rs:212-218, 522-539 (stored); vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/commands.rs:1370-1400 (only fired by the JS trigger_alert_hook API); vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/mod.rs:4094-4114 on_script_error -> stop() at 2182
evidence: The hook is stored but never called when a script error occurs. Instead on_script_error logs it and calls stop(), which halts playback for the whole movie. In Director the hook would swallow the error, the failing handler would abort, and the game would keep running. So under dirplayer any remaining unimplemented-feature error stops the game outright, where the real player would carry on (possibly with a glitch). The error strings would also differ from Director's.

name: centerStage
game_usage: Wrapper timeout setup sets centerStage to 0 in startMovie (plugin mode included).
dirplayer: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/mod.rs:4017-4023 (stores and dispatches a stage-size-changed event with center=false), 3879
evidence: Stored. Director ignores it in the Shockwave plugin, where the stage fills the embed. dirplayer forwards center=false to the JS stage-size callback, which in its own dev UI (src/vm/callbacks.ts:220) left-aligns the canvas container; the polyfill embed used by public/index.html is not visibly affected.

name: clickOn
game_usage: In mouseUp the generic buttons check that the clicked sprite is themselves and otherwise exit: the robotwars/lobby 'Jump' navigation buttons (factory top tabs ch71/73/74 use it), the factory 'popup menu' weapon slots, the login 'Buttonscript' buttons, and the IRC room list.
evidence: Director documents `the clickOn` as the last ACTIVE sprite clicked, meaning one that has a sprite or cast-member script. dirplayer stores the front-most sprite of any kind (scripted=false; the comment there says so on purpose). Mouse events are delivered to the front-most SCRIPTED sprite (mouse_down_sprite, commands.rs:727). So when an unscripted label or overlay sits over a scripted button, the button gets mouseUp but sees clickOn equal to the overlay and exits: the click does nothing. Also, because of the patch, 3D sprites are hit-tested first (score.rs:5987-5990). I checked factory frame 5: the top tabs ch71/73/74 (shape 1/97) are front-most at their rects, so this does NOT explain the workshop tabs there. It is still a likely cause for any button the game stacks under a label. Confirm Director's rule (active-only) in Adobe's code.

name: currentSpriteNum
game_usage: Read in about 70 behaviors (almost always in beginSprite, to cache the sprite channel; also in mouse handlers to set the cursor or forward mouse events to the sprite one channel below). One use is in a movie script: the robotwars 'Money Manager' buy handler, called from the factory buy buttons' mouseUp, uses it to message the sprite one channel below the clicked button.
evidence: Inside a behavior it reads the receiver instance's spriteNum, which matches Director for all the behavior uses. A movie-script handler has no receiver, so the value falls back to member_script_sprite_num (only set while a cast-member script runs), then to click_on_sprite: the front-most sprite of ANY kind under the last mouseDown. Director gives the sprite whose event is being dispatched. The two agree only when the clicked buy button is the front-most sprite at the click point. In factory frame 104 the buy button (ch44) is overlapped by higher channels (e.g. ch79, a 259x211 panel), depending on registration points. To settle it, log `the currentSpriteNum` inside the buy handler in Director, or check the overlap in dirplayer for frames 101-178.

name: debugPlaybackEnabled

evidence: Stored and read back. In Director it only opens a message window, which has no gameplay effect, so this is enough.

evidence: Get returns 0 and set is accepted. Projector-only path, and the property has no meaning in a browser.

name: frame
game_usage: Overwhelmingly go(the frame) to hold the playhead (69x) and go(the frame + 1) to step (20x); a few equality tests against fixed frame numbers in garage/lobby state logic. Never read inside a tell block.
dirplayer: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/movie.rs:247; vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/mod.rs:3671-3697 (tell film-loop override); go() sets next_frame, current_frame changes only on advance: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/mod.rs:2064-2100
evidence: Returns movie.current_frame. go() only queues next_frame, so the frame keeps reading the current frame until the playhead actually moves, as in Director. When go() takes effect relative to the rest of the event dispatch is a machinery:go question, not this property. Correction: go() to a DIFFERENT frame is not just queued. MovieHandlers::go (vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/handlers/movie.rs:375-520) runs endSprite, advance_frame and beginSprite inline, so `the frame` read later in the same handler already returns the new frame. The game's go(the frame) holds are unaffected; see machinery:go-navigation.

name: itemDelimiter
game_usage: Saved, set to one character (TAB, '.', ':', '=', '@', '_', SPACE), then restored, to split robot maps (TAB), main.ini lines, IRC nick/host parts, IP strings and lobby data.
dirplayer: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/movie.rs:221 (get), :500-501 (set); player/bytecode/string.rs:296-323 and :356-392 (chunk exprs take movie.item_delimiter); player/bytecode/get_set.rs:982-987 (last item)
evidence: The getter returns the one-character string. The setter keeps the first character. Every chunk path (get/put/delete, `the last item`, count) reads movie.item_delimiter at the time of the operation. Movie is built once (player/mod.rs:860, Movie::empty), so the setting survives movie switches like a Player property. Edge case: setting it to EMPTY would panic on `.unwrap()` (movie.rs:501), but the game only assigns one-character values or values it saved earlier.

game_usage: Read in keyDown/keyUp handlers. In the arena (backyard and main frame scripts) keyUp switches the camera with 0-3/v/b and starts chat with T. In the factory, 'z' means undo. The login and chat fields test RETURN, TAB, BACKSPACE and QUOTE, and insert the typed character into the field text.
evidence: Fixed 2026-10-23. the key / the keyCode are the last key pressed (ScummVM, tested against Director, sets them on key-down only). Verified in game: with Up held, pressing 2/3/1 changes the follow camera distance 500->1000->1500->500.

name: keyboardFocusSprite
game_usage: Set in login (RETURN/TAB moves focus to a field a few channels on; the 'new user' panel focuses its first field, or 0 when hidden) and in the arena chat line (makes the field editable and focuses it, then 0 after sending).
dirplayer: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/mod.rs:3983-3987 (set: plain store, "TODO switch focus"), :3241-3243 (get); player/commands.rs:690-713 (focus on click)
evidence: The setter stores the channel, and keyboard routing reads it, so keys go to the new field and 0 removes focus. Not done: no caret or selection placement in the newly focused field, and no blur/focus side effects. Director puts the caret somewhere on a programmatic focus change, probably the end or a select-all. The login Filter behavior sets selStart itself, which hides this there. Settle it with Adobe's code or a reference capture of where the caret lands.

name: keyCode

evidence: The JS-to-Mac table gives arrows 123/126/124/125, tab 48, backspace 51, letters and digits on Mac codes. Navigation keys are matched by name to 115/116/117/119/121. Every code the game tests is produced. It shares current_key() with `the key`, so it has the same held-key issue, but the game only reads it in keyDown, where the key just pressed is the last one down.

evidence: `the last char in s` compiles to `get 0` with id 12. Ids up to 0x0b are movie props, so 12 takes the last-chunk branch: 12-0x0b = 1 = Char, which returns the final character (or "" for an empty string).

name: maxinteger
game_usage: Used as "never" (negative maxinteger as an initial last-refresh time, timeout period for a do-nothing persistent timeout) and in the MD5 routine (maxinteger + 1 must wrap to the minimum integer) whose digest verifies robot data from main.asp.
dirplayer: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/movie.rs:354; integer add vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/datum_operations.rs:181 and player/bytecode/arithmetics.rs:26-27 (plain i32 +, release build has overflow checks off so it wraps)
evidence: Returns 2147483647 as in Director. maxinteger + 1 wraps to -2147483648 as Director 32-bit integers do (release profile, no overflow-checks), so the MD5 matches; robot checksums verify in practice.

name: milliSeconds
game_usage: Read everywhere as a monotonic ms clock: lag/ping stamps, send times, timers (20 s renderer warning wait, door/news timers), seeding randomSeed, and the arena checkTempo anti-speedhack: elapsed ms per systemDate second, plus a busy-wait loop on the clock that only runs when a speed hack was detected.
evidence: Returns ms since player start (Utc now minus system_start_time) as Int; Director documents ms since the computer/player started, and the game only uses differences. Reading it sets input_polled so a busy-wait repeat loop yields cooperatively (timing of that yield is covered under machinery:tempo). Int wraps after ~24 days, irrelevant.

name: mouseH

evidence: Returns mouse_loc.x in stage coordinates, which is the documented meaning. Clicks and moves are converted from canvas to movie coordinates before they are stored (score.rs comment at get_concrete_sprite_render_rect). Off-stage values during a drag that leaves the canvas depend on browser pointer capture, which is minor.

evidence: Returns point(mouse_loc). pointToLine and locToLine themselves belong to another slice.

dirplayer: vendor/dirplayer-rs/vm-rust/src/player/bytecode/get_set.rs:1012-1040 (anim2 prop 0x02 with castLib); player/cast_lib.rs:357-365 (max member id)
evidence: Returns the highest member slot number in use, which is Director's documented meaning (the number of the last cast member), so a loop reaches every populated slot.

evidence: TRUE while Alt or AltGraph is down. Developer-only path.

game_usage: contains "Windows"/"Macintosh" picks the key-filter tables for login text input and gates a projector-only browserName setup.
evidence: Returns "Windows,32", Director's Win32 string; the Windows branches run.

name: preferred3dRenderer
game_usage: Only assigned: the login wrapper picks #directx9/#directX5_2/#openGL/#software from getRendererServices, and arena/garage frame scripts reapply a saved global preference. Never read.
evidence: Set is accepted and ignored; dirplayer has a single WebGL2 renderer, so there is nothing to switch, and the game never reads the property back.

name: productVersion
game_usage: Wrapper enterFullscreen only: checks whether char 3 is "." to choose D10+ window APIs.
evidence: Returns "11.0" (char 3 is "."), so the D10+ branch would be taken, as with the real 10.1/11 players. Only reached in projector mode anyway.

name: randomSeed
game_usage: Saved, set to a constant, used to drive random(256) as a keystream for a reversible XOR obfuscation of ammo counters, user data and local prefs, then restored. The ASP object also saves it, reseeds from the clock to make a unique request id, and restores it.
evidence: Setting it makes random() deterministic, and the obfuscation only ever round-trips inside this player, so encrypt/decrypt agree. Divergence: before any seed is set dirplayer reports 0 (Director reports the clock-derived seed). The game's save/restore idiom then installs seed 0, so after the first ASP request or ammo update every later random() follows the same LCG sequence in every session, where Director would differ per run. Only cosmetic randomness (debris offsets, camera shake) is affected. The PRNG algorithm itself differs from Director's (dirplayer comment admits it); that only matters if a value produced by real Director had to be decoded, which does not happen here.

name: runMode
game_usage: Compared (case-insensitively) to "Plugin"/"plugin"/"Author" to choose net vs file loading of main.ini, gotoNetMovie vs go, and to skip author-only debug paths; the wrapper caches it in a global.
evidence: Returns "Plugin" unless overridden, which is what a Shockwave browser player reports; the game then takes its plugin branches (main.ini via getNetText, gotoNetMovie), which is the intended browser path.

name: safePlayer
game_usage: Wrapper UPnP setup: proceeds only if safePlayer is 0 and the UPnP Xtra exists; that only runs when main.ini enables UPnP.
evidence: Returns FALSE (0), Director's default. server/index.mjs:62 sends upnpenabled=false, so the UPnP path is never reached.

name: selEnd
game_usage: Same login editing behaviors as selStart: collapse the selection to one end, extend it by one, and read it to compute insertion and delete ranges.
evidence: Same defect as selStart: the setter takes the start from player.text_selection_start, the last Lingo-set value, not the live caret. So `set the selEnd to the selStart` after a mouse click or drag selection moves the caret to an old position. The getter is correct.

name: selStart
game_usage: Login fields: the 'Horizontal scroll (field)' and 'Filter Input Characters' behaviors and the password behavior read and set the selection to do their own editing: caret moves, insert, delete, and collapsing the selection to one end.
evidence: Reading is live from the focused member, which is correct. Setting one end calls sync_focused_text_selection, which rebuilds BOTH ends from player.text_selection_start/end. Those fields are only updated by Lingo sets and some editor paths, not by mouse caret placement or drag selection (cast_member.rs:348/462 write the member's sel_* only). So after the user clicks or drags in a field, `set the selStart to the selEnd` (collapse right) or `set the selEnd to the selStart` (collapse left, used on left arrow) mixes in a stale other end. Director keeps the live other end. Normal typing works because the behavior sets selStart before selEnd.

name: stage
game_usage: Wrapper only: reads and re-assigns (the stage).rect from a timeout target's stopMovie (a stage-rect nudge on every movie switch), enterFullscreen(the stage) and (the stage).type = #dialog, the last two only in projector mode or with alwaysontop set in main.ini.
evidence: rect get/set is implemented and writing back the same rect is a no-op resize. `.type` is not settable (it would raise "Cannot set stage property type"), but that path needs alwaysontop in main.ini, and server/index.mjs:61 sends false. The fullscreen path is projector-only.

name: stillDown
game_usage: Tested in mouseEnter/mouseWithin/mouseLeave handlers so the hover cursor is not changed during a drag, and in a few scroll/drag behaviors. Not used as a busy-wait loop.
evidence: TRUE between mouseDown and mouseUp, as documented. input_polled is set, so any polling loop would yield.

name: systemDate
game_usage: Arena (Training and multiplayer frame scripts): the date object's .seconds is read at start and every 5 frames by checkTempo. Each time it increases the game measures ms elapsed and flags a speed hack if over 15 s. The multiplayer frame script also uses this seconds value for the 20 s opponent-silence walkover and ping time.
evidence: Fixed 2026-10-23. date .seconds now counts from midnight (Director's documented value; a read gave 48006 at 13:20). The arena's pacing and walkover timer only act when it grows, so it stalled at each minute.
